bundle.scope: Vite initial entry dependency closure, largest lazy JavaScript chunk and Workbox precache from the production build.

asyncChunk.scope: Largest JavaScript file referenced by the Vite manifest outside the initial dependency closure.

exempt.reason: The largest-lazy-chunk budget asks whether a route chunk is getting fat, and the error reporter is not a route: it is fetched once the page is idle, is excluded from the offline precache, and never blocks a paint. Measured at 27 022 bytes gzip with default integrations off and __SENTRY_DEBUG__/__SENTRY_TRACING__ defined false; the same code with Sentry’s defaults measures 154 402. The 30 000 ceiling is that measurement plus room for a patch release, and it is a real gate: it fails if the reporter grows, which is the only question this exemption still has to answer.

pwaPrecache.scope: Files referenced by Workbox precacheAndRoute in dist/sw.js; byte count uses emitted file sizes before transfer compression.
pwaPrecache.rebaselineReason: V4.2 ships four font files on purpose: DM Sans 600/700, which the stylesheet already asked for and font-synthesis: none prevented the browser from faking, and Plus Jakarta Sans 600/700 as the display face. Measured against the V4.1 baseline this left one entry of headroom, so an unrelated asset would have failed the gate and invited a hurried raise. Re-measured at the V4.2 design commit; the 10% allowance still guards accidental growth from here.

totalDiagnostic.scope: Every JavaScript and CSS file emitted below dist, including dynamic chunks, PWA files and public research assets. This total is NOT what a visitor downloads: it grows mechanically with every route split into a lazy chunk, which is to say every time the splitting improves. The budgets that protect the experience are elsewhere — initial closure and largest lazy chunk — and are unchanged.
totalDiagnostic.rebaselineReason: Raised from 260 000 to 300 000 for two additions, kept separate because they are not the same kind of thing. 877 bytes come from the Stripe checkout merge (#128), which had already put this diagnostic 877 bytes over before any Sentry work. 26 769 bytes are the Sentry reporter chunk, which this total counts because it counts everything emitted — while the budgets that protect the experience do not: the reporter is excluded from the offline precache and never enters the initial closure, which moved by 465 bytes. A diagnostic that is permanently red stops being read, so it is re-set rather than left to shout; the headroom above 287 646 is deliberately small so the next growth still shows.
